summary: Retest of the iteration 28 card-payment fixes. Regression suites pass: test_statement_card_pay.py and test_invoices_hst.py, 37/37. New suite test_card_pay_fixes.py: 3/5 pass. Three real Stripe payments were completed with card 4242 in Playwright, plus one more with the portal's settle request blocked. HIGH: the double-charge fix does NOT work. The Emergent Stripe proxy returns '404 page not found' for POST /v1/checkout/sessions/{id}/expire. invoices_checkout catches that error and logs a warning, so old session A stays 'open' in db.payment_sessions and stays open and payable at Stripe. I paid B (CA$18.08 for DL-000001+2) and then paid the old session A (CA$18.08 again): the merchant was really charged twice. The other fixes work. (1) Safety net: paying A recorded credit 18.08 and credit_invoices [DL-000001, DL-000002], GET /payments/A returns {status: paid, credit: 18.08}, the toast reads 'PAYMENT RECEIVED · CA$18.08 WAS ALREADY PAID · DASHLOCAL WILL REFUND IT', and the invoices show as paid once (paid total CA$18.08). (2) Settle-first: for a session paid at Stripe but never settled, a new checkout for [that invoice + a fresh one] settled the old session, marked the invoice paid and charged only the fresh one (CA$11.30). A checkout for only already-paid-but-unsettled invoices returned 400 'These invoices were just paid'. (3) A cs_test_fake session returns 424 'Couldn't reach the card processor', not 500. A broken old session does not block a new checkout. (4) ?paid=<sid> and ?paid=cancel each show the toast once, the param is removed from the URL, and a reload shows no toast. (5) Admin reset cleared payment_sessions (0 left). (6) The select button reads SELECT TO PAY / SELECTED TO PAY, testID invoice-select-DL-000001, 338x56.

critical.issue: Old open sessions are not closed. stripe.checkout.Session.expire gets HTTP 404 '404 page not found' from https://integrations.emergentagent.com/stripe/v1/checkout/sessions/{id}/expire, which the proxy does not support. The except block at server.py:3953 only logs 'Could not close old checkout', so the DB status stays 'open' and the Stripe session stays payable. Reproduced: paid B, then paid old A, and the card was charged twice (pi_3UUXDAFz2w4mYLKz02B2UVPD).

minor.issue: If Stripe reports payment_status 'paid' but amount_total differs from amount_cents, nothing is recorded or alerted. A paid session would stay 'open' with no warning.
If settle_session raises for an old session (Stripe unreachable), the loop logs a warning and still creates a new session. Two payable sessions then exist for the same invoices.

action_items: HIGH: the Emergent Stripe proxy does not support Session.expire (404), so the double charge is still possible. Do not rely on expire. Options: (a) if an open session already covers exactly the same invoice ids and amount, return its existing url (stripe.checkout.Session.retrieve(sid).url works through the proxy) instead of creating a new one. (b) If the invoice sets differ, refuse with 400 ('finish or cancel your earlier card checkout') or keep the expire attempt but pass expires_at=now+30min (Stripe's minimum) on every Session.create so stale sessions die quickly. (c) Keep the credit/refund safety net, which works. (d) Don't treat a failed expire as success; the session must stay tracked so settle/credit still runs.
Minor: in settle_session, log or alert the admin when payment_status is 'paid' but amount_total != amount_cents.

After the fix, rerun backend/tests/test_card_pay_fixes.py. TestOldSessionsClosed currently fails 2 tests on exactly this bug. If you choose reuse or block instead of expire, update those 2 assertions to match the new behaviour.

rca_of_issue: Repro: seed, then POST checkout [DL1,DL2] -> A, then the same again -> B. The backend log shows a POST to the proxy .../checkout/sessions/A/expire returning 404 'page not found', then 'Could not close old checkout'. db A stays 'open'. Stripe retrieve(A).status is 'open'. Paying B and then A's URL both succeed. Root cause: the Emergent Stripe proxy does not route the expire endpoint, and the code treats the failure as non-fatal. Mitigation: reuse or block an existing open session instead of expiring it, and set a short expires_at on create.
